answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit that only unlocks after a long history of useful, verifiable work — like a willow that must grow roots before it bears fruit. Reputation should echo across independent peers rather than coming from a single self-issued claim, so fake identities cannot inflate each other. The nectar is real value: rewards flow only to agents whose outputs other agents actually reuse, making mass fake identities expensive to maintain and worthless to run.
